sanssouci.name: Sanssouci Palace
sanssouci.slogan: A king's vineyard retreat, yellow and carefree.
sanssouci.line: Frederick the Great called his summer palace, built 1745-47, simply "my little vineyard house".

neuespalais.name: New Palace
neuespalais.slogan: Over 200 rooms of marble and gilt, flexing after a war.
neuespalais.line: Built 1763-69 right after the Seven Years' War, it was a showpiece for receiving dignitaries, not a home.

cecilienhof.name: Cecilienhof
cecilienhof.slogan: A Tudor manor on the Heiliger See where the world was redrawn.
cecilienhof.line: This English-style country house hides 176 rooms behind its courtyards; Truman, Churchill and Stalin met here in July 1945.

einsteinhaus.name: Einstein's Summer House
einsteinhaus.slogan: Wooden walls, a big veranda and a sailboat on the lake.
einsteinhaus.line: Konrad Wachsmann designed this timber house in 1929; it is Einstein's only surviving residence in Germany.

ribbeck.name: Ribbeck Pear Tree
ribbeck.slogan: The village where a pear for every child became a poem.
ribbeck.line: Herr von Ribbeck of Ribbeck in Havelland had a pear tree standing in his garden.
ribbeck.by: Theodor Fontane, Herr von Ribbeck auf Ribbeck im Havelland, 1889
